solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Food parcel and document a courier carries (4)

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer inside it, as a courier holds a package

annotation.surface: A courier brings a food delivery along with some paperwork.
annotation.walkthrough: The courier is not a substitution for anything; the words themselves carry the answer across their joins.
annotation.definitionFit: A taco is a folded tortilla wrapped around a filling, a small parcel of food.

entries.clue: Empty Argentine boxing club in decline (5)

indicators.note: remove the insides, leaving only the outer letters
the club is enclosed by the other letters

annotation.surface: An Argentine boxing club is losing members and fading away.
annotation.walkthrough: Boxing reads as the sport, and club as a gym; the club is the thing held and the Argentine only lends its first and last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a storm or fever that abates dies down, just as it would decline.

entries.clue: Blown instrument in old car by hot area (7)

indicators.note: placed next to, so the pieces follow one another

blocks.note: hot in the sense of fashionable, in

annotation.surface: Someone plays a wind instrument in an old car parked in a sunny spot.
annotation.walkthrough: Hot here means fashionable, which gives IN, not a temperature.
annotation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument played by blowing.

entries.clue: Period with old chap suited high-flying lady (10)

blocks.note: a space of time is a period

annotation.surface: A woman spends a spell dating an old gentleman who suits her well.
annotation.walkthrough: Suited looks like it means well matched to the chap; it belongs to the definition, describing someone in a spacesuit.
annotation.definitionFit: A spacewoman wears a spacesuit and flies higher than anyone.

entries.clue: Nerve gas released outside cold roadside diner? (9)

indicators.note: the letters are let loose and rearranged
the rearranged letters go around C

annotation.surface: A nerve gas leaks out beside a chilly roadside café.
annotation.walkthrough: A roadside diner sounds like a café, but it is a creature eating roadkill; the question mark flags the joke.
annotation.definitionFit: A scavenger, such as a crow, feeds on dead animals found beside roads.

entries.clue: A time without profits can be challenging (7)

definitions.note: Challenging is a participle; against is a preposition, but both express opposition in phrases like 'against the ruling'.

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so A and T sit around the profits

annotation.surface: A period with no earnings can make life hard.
annotation.walkthrough: Without reads as lacking, but here it means outside: A and T wrap around GAINS.
annotation.definitionFit: Against means opposing, as in challenging a proposal.

entries.clue: Wield authority, but not whilst holding power (5)

indicators.note: the word appears only when it no longer has P inside

blocks.note: an authority on a subject is an expert

annotation.surface: Someone may wield authority, but only when out of office.
annotation.walkthrough: Wield authority looks like one phrase; wield alone is the definition and authority is the expert.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym when the object is power or influence: you can wield it or exert it.

entries.clue: Job vacancy in Split? (7)

blocks.note: a post waiting to be filled
a split as a noun: a crack or gap

annotation.surface: A job is advertised in Split, the Croatian port city.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital S makes Split look like the Croatian city; it is really a gap or crack.
annotation.definitionFit: An opening is both a vacant position and a gap.

entries.clue: Retired volunteers given samples and vouchers (9)

indicators.note: going back, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: TA, the Territorial Army of volunteer soldiers, reversed
testers are samples, as of perfume

annotation.surface: Retired volunteers are handed product samples and discount coupons.
annotation.walkthrough: Vouchers looks like coupons, matching samples; it means people who vouch for something. The TA was Britain's reserve army of part-time volunteers.
annotation.definitionFit: Attesters vouch for the truth of something, so they are vouchers.

entries.clue: Cream tea’s a tad unusual in a region of Chile (7,6)

indicators.note: the letters are put into an unusual order

annotation.surface: A cream tea tastes slightly odd when served somewhere in Chile.
annotation.walkthrough: A cream tea is a British afternoon snack of scones with clotted cream and jam.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by location: this bone-dry plateau covers much of northern Chile.

entries.clue: Corrupt news chief to turn over documents (6)

indicators.note: the editor's letters are flipped

annotation.surface: A crooked newspaper editor hands over incriminating papers.
annotation.walkthrough: Corrupt looks like an adjective describing the chief; it is the verb, to spoil.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: both mean to make something pure foul or tainted.

entries.clue: Most whacky fan one’s seen during match (8)

indicators.note: the letter appears within the match

blocks.note: a Test is an international cricket match

annotation.surface: The wildest supporter is spotted at the game.
annotation.walkthrough: A Test match is a long international cricket game.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the superlative: nutty and whacky are both informal words for crazy.

entries.clue: Reliable hand? (8)

blocks.note: honest and dependable, as in a trustworthy dealer
a poker hand of five cards in sequence

annotation.surface: A dependable helper, a trusty pair of hands.
annotation.walkthrough: Reliable hand reads as a good worker; hand is really a set of playing cards.
annotation.definitionFit: Straight describes someone honest, and names a poker hand.

entries.clue: Dine later, after knocking together batter (9)

indicators.note: the letters are roughly assembled into a new word

annotation.surface: We'll eat later, once the pancake batter has been mixed.
annotation.walkthrough: Batter sounds like the pancake mixture; it is a cricketer. A tail-ender is one of the weakest batsmen, who bat last in the order.
annotation.definitionFit: A tail-ender is a batter who comes in near the end of a cricket innings.

entries.clue: Line manager one suspended after losing head (6)

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: something that dangles hangs suspended; lose the D

annotation.surface: A line manager is suspended from work after being sacked as head.
annotation.walkthrough: Line manager suggests an office boss; it is someone managing a fishing line.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: someone fishing controls a line, so is jokingly its manager.

entries.clue: A tiny path somehow is something to be avoided (9)

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in some other way

annotation.surface: A narrow little footpath is best steered clear of.
annotation.walkthrough: Something to be avoided reads as describing the path; it stands alone as the definition, with is as a link.
annotation.definitionFit: An antipathy is a strong dislike, or the object of one, a thing you avoid.

entries.clue: Resentful model dumping soprano for bishop (6)

indicators.note: to dump something is to throw it away, so the soprano's letter is discarded from the word
for in the sense of in exchange for, so the bishop's letter is swapped in

blocks.note: a sitter poses for an artist
chess notation for bishop; replaces S

annotation.surface: A model is sore after being dropped from the choir for a bishop.
annotation.walkthrough: Model suggests a catwalk; here it is someone who sits for a painter. B for bishop comes from chess notation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone bitter about a snub harbours resentment over it.

entries.clue: One casting series collared by Oscarless extra (7)

indicators.note: held inside, as by a collar
the O (Oscar in the NATO alphabet) is taken out

blocks.note: OTHER, meaning extra, without its O
a row is a series, placed inside THER

annotation.surface: A director casting a film keeps hiring the same extra who never won an Oscar.
annotation.walkthrough: Casting suggests a film director picking actors; here it means hurling. Oscar is the NATO alphabet word for O.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to cast is to throw, so one casting is one throwing.

entries.clue: Dickens fan? (8)

blocks.note: the surface wants the novelist; the setter means 'the dickens', an old euphemism for the devil
an admirer, here a devotee or worshipper

annotation.surface: An admirer of the novelist Charles Dickens.
annotation.walkthrough: Dickens reads as the novelist, but 'the dickens', as in 'what the dickens?', is a mild word for the devil, so a fan of it worships Satan.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: a follower of Satan is literally a fan of the dickens.

entries.clue: Reportedly lacking in strength, but cunning (7)

definitions.note: Cunning is read as the noun, meaning craftiness.

indicators.note: as it is said, so it sounds like the word

annotation.surface: Someone is said to be weak but crafty.
annotation.walkthrough: Cunning looks like an adjective, but sleight is the noun, meaning craft or dexterity, as in sleight of hand.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the noun sense: craft and dexterous trickery, as in sleight of hand.

entries.clue: Small issue vasectomy surgeons initially ignored (7)

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: a vasectomy is known as the snip; lose the S

annotation.surface: A minor complaint that vasectomy surgeons brushed aside at first.
annotation.walkthrough: Small issue reads as a trivial matter; issue here means offspring. Nippers is British slang for small children.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: young children are nippers, and issue is a formal word for offspring.

entries.clue: Drop dead shortly after drinking last of beer (8)

indicators.note: cut short by its last letter
a drinker takes something inside, so the word swallows the letter
the last of anything is its final part, here the final letter

blocks.note: final letter of beeR, placed inside

annotation.surface: Someone collapses and dies soon after finishing a pint.
annotation.walkthrough: Drop dead looks like one phrase; drop alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fall in prices can be called a drop or a lowering.

entries.clue: A story about Elvis essentially still going strong? (5)

indicators.note: about in its sense of around, so the story wraps the letter
the essence or centre of the word

blocks.note: a lie is a made-up story
middle letter of elVis, inside LIE

annotation.surface: A rumour claims Elvis Presley never died and lives on.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the rumour that Elvis is still alive, a story told about him.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose paraphrase, hence the question mark: still going strong means still living and active.

entries.clue: One rooted for the general public, not the posh (6)

indicators.note: U, the letter for upper class, is removed

annotation.surface: Someone backed by ordinary people rather than the upper classes.
annotation.walkthrough: One rooted for looks like someone cheered on; rooted means planted, a tree. U is the old label for upper-class usage.
annotation.definitionFit: A poplar is a tree, something with roots.

entries.clue: Lorry is extremely cold (-1C) (5)

indicators.note: minus one C, so one C comes out

annotation.surface: A lorry reports freezing weather: minus one degree Celsius.
annotation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like a temperature reading; it means take away one C. An artic is British slang for an articulated lorry.
annotation.definitionFit: A British informal short form: the articulated lorry, with a separate cab and trailer, is called an artic.

entries.clue: Don’t ring sweet fools in the British government (7,6)

indicators.note: the letters are fooled around with, jumbled

annotation.surface: An instruction not to phone the sugary dessert, fools, at the heart of government.
annotation.walkthrough: Sweet fools looks like a dessert (a fool is a fruit and cream pudding); fools is the anagram indicator. Downing Street houses the Prime Minister.
annotation.definitionFit: Metonymy: the London street where the Prime Minister lives and works stands for the government itself.

entries.clue: I turn and reply improperly in a salacious way (10)

indicators.note: the letters are not in their proper order

annotation.surface: Someone turns and answers back with a lewd remark.
annotation.walkthrough: Improperly fits the surface as rude behaviour, but it signals the letters are rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Pruriently means with an unhealthy interest in sex, salaciously.

entries.clue: If temperature’s dropped, endure suffering cold? (4)

indicators.note: something dropped is let go, so the letter leaves the word

blocks.note: to stick something out is to endure it

annotation.surface: When the fever falls, you can put up with having a cold.
annotation.walkthrough: Suffering cold looks like part of the wordplay; it is the definition, someone ill with a cold, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, hence the question mark: having a cold is one way of being ill.
